# Exporting Log Data to Amazon S3

## Overview

An export task can export all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group named my-log-group to an Amazon S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket. Exporting log data to S3 buckets that are encrypted by AWS KMS is supported, but exporting to buckets encrypted with DSSE-KMS is not. The details of how you set up the export depend on whether the Amazon S3 bucket is in the same account as the logs being exported or in a different account.

## Bucket requirements

AWS recommends using a bucket that was created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. If you want to use an existing bucket, you can skip the bucket creation procedure. The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export, because CloudWatch Logs doesn't support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region.

## Required permissions

To create the export task, you must be signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role and with the permissions logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams, and logs:DescribeLogGroups. Creating an export task requires signing in with sufficient permissions as documented in the access permissions section.

## Setting access permissions on the bucket (same-account export)

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and any objects it contains by default. The resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

AWS now requires you to specify the list of source accounts that are allowed to export log data to your S3 bucket. The account IDs in the aws:SourceAccount key are the accounts from which a user can export log data to your S3 bucket. The aws:SourceArn key is the resource for which the action is being taken and may be restricted to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the S3 bucket is created, to allow export within the same account.

Create the bucket policy file with a text editor, not the IAM console. The put-bucket-policy command then sets the access policy that enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to your S3 bucket. The bucket owner will have full permissions on all of the exported objects.

If the existing bucket already has policies attached, you should add the CloudWatch Logs access statements to those policies. AWS recommends evaluating the resulting set of permissions to be sure they are appropriate for the users who will access the bucket.

## Exporting to a bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS

The SSE-KMS procedure is necessary only if you are exporting to an S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. The KMS key policy must allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal logs.Region.amazonaws.com to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

The aws kms create-key command with key_policy.json creates the KMS key. The aws s3api put-bucket-encryption command then applies the bucketencryption.json configuration to the bucket using the aws:kms SSE algorithm with BucketKeyEnabled set to true. If the put-bucket-encryption command doesn't return an error, the process is successful.

## Cross-account export

For cross-account export, you must first create a new IAM policy enabling CloudWatch Logs to have the s3:PutObject action for the destination bucket in the destination account. This policy has two conditional additions:

# Exporting CloudWatch Logs data to Amazon S3

## Before you begin

- A CloudWatch Logs log group to export. This guide uses a log group named my-log-group. No steps are given here for creating it.

## Overview

An export task can export all data from the CloudWatch Logs log group named my-log-group to an Amazon S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket. Exporting log data to S3 buckets that are encrypted by AWS KMS is supported, but exporting to buckets encrypted with DSSE-KMS is not. The details of how you set up the export depend on whether the Amazon S3 bucket is in the same account as the logs being exported or in a different account.

## The bucket and Region

AWS recommends using a bucket that was created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. If you want to use an existing bucket, you can skip the bucket creation procedure. The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export. Because of this, CloudWatch Logs doesn't support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region.

## Permissions to create the export task

To create the export task, you must be signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role and with the permissions logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams, and logs:DescribeLogGroups. Creating an export task requires signing in with sufficient permissions as documented in this access permissions section, and this must happen before you run the command that creates the task.

## Setting the bucket access policy

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and any objects it contains by default. Because they are private, the resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

AWS now requires you to specify the list of source accounts that are allowed to export log data to your S3 bucket. The account IDs in the aws:SourceAccount key are the accounts from which a user can export log data to your S3 bucket. The aws:SourceArn key is the resource for which the action is being taken and may be restricted to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the S3 bucket is created, to allow export within the same account.

Create the bucket policy file with a text editor, not the IAM console. The put-bucket-policy command sets the access policy that enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to your S3 bucket. It works only when the access policy has been written (the resource owner granting access) and the list of source accounts has been specified. The bucket owner will have full permissions on all of the exported objects.

If the existing bucket already has policies attached, you should add the CloudWatch Logs access statements to those policies. AWS recommends evaluating the resulting set of permissions to be sure they are appropriate for the users who will access the bucket.

## SSE-KMS encryption (optional)

Because exporting to KMS-encrypted buckets is supported, an SSE-KMS procedure is available. It is necessary only if you are exporting to an S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. In that case, the KMS key policy must allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal logs.Region.amazonaws.com to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

The aws kms create-key command with key_policy.json creates the KMS key. The aws s3api put-bucket-encryption command applies the bucketencryption.json configuration to the bucket using the aws:kms SSE algorithm with BucketKeyEnabled set to true. If the put-bucket-encryption command doesn't return an error, the process is successful.

## Cross-account export

For cross-account export, you must first create a new IAM policy enabling CloudWatch Logs to have the s3:PutObject action for the destination bucket in the destination account. If the destination bucket uses KMS encryption, this IAM policy must add the kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt actions for the key resource. If ACLs are enabled on the destination bucket, it must add the s3:PutObjectAcl action.

To create an export task in this case, you must be signed in with an IAM role that has the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy attached, the IAM policy you created, and the logs permissions.

The cross-account bucket policy includes a statement allowing an IAM role in the exporting account to perform s3:PutObject with the s3:x-amz-acl condition bucket-owner-full-control. For cross-account SSE-KMS export, the KMS key policy must also allow the IAM role used for creating the export task to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

## Creating the export task

The create-export-task command creates the export task and returns a taskId. For a cross-account export, it succeeds only when both the new IAM policy enabling CloudWatch Logs to perform s3:PutObject (with the additional actions above where they apply) has been created and you are signed in with the role that has the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy, that IAM policy, and the logs permissions. After you create an export task, it might take anywhere from a few seconds to a few hours, depending on the size of the data to export.

# Logging Protection Pack (Web ACL) Traffic to Amazon S3

You are charged for logging in addition to the charges for using AWS WAF.

## Setting up the bucket

To send protection pack (web ACL) traffic logs to Amazon S3, you set up an Amazon S3 bucket from the same account as you use to manage the protection pack (web ACL). You name the bucket starting with aws-waf-logs-. Bucket names for AWS WAF logging must start with aws-waf-logs- and can end with any suffix you want. When you enable logging in AWS WAF, you provide the bucket name. If you use prefixes in your object keys name, you can provide your prefixes in your logging bucket names. Specifying prefixes in the logging bucket name is not available through the console; use the AWS WAF APIs, CLI, or AWS CloudFormation instead.

You can access and analyze your Amazon S3 logs using the Amazon Athena interactive query service.

## Encryption

AWS WAF supports encryption with Amazon S3 buckets for key type Amazon S3 key (SSE-S3) and for AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) AWS KMS keys. AWS WAF doesn't support encryption for AWS Key Management Service keys that are managed by AWS.

## Log file delivery and format

Log files from your protection pack (web ACL) are published to the Amazon S3 bucket at 5-minute intervals. Each log file contains log records for the traffic recorded in the previous 5 minutes. Multiple log files may be published within a 5-minute period, and the log files may contain some or all of the AWS WAF log records for the traffic recorded in the previous five minutes. A single log file contains interleaved entries with multiple records.

The log files are compressed. If you open the log files using the Amazon S3 console, Amazon S3 decompresses the log records and displays them. If you download the log files, you must decompress them to view the records.

AWS WAF logs are written under a folder structure determined by account ID, Region, protection pack (web ACL) name, and date and time. The time specifications in the folder structure and log file name adhere to the timestamp format YYYYMMddTHHmmZ.

## Required permissions

Configuring protection pack (web ACL) traffic logging for an Amazon S3 bucket requires specific permissions settings. The required logging permissions are set for you when you use the AWSWAFConsoleFullAccess or AWSWAFFullAccess managed policies. The logging permissions must be attached to the user that you use to manage AWS WAF. When you set the listed permissions, you might see access denied errors in your AWS CloudTrail logs, but the permissions are correct for AWS WAF logging. A Resource setting of "*" permits actions on all AWS resources that each action supports.

## Bucket policy and ownership

By default, Amazon S3 buckets and the objects they contain are private, and only the bucket owner can access them. If the user creating the log owns the bucket, the service automatically attaches a policy to the bucket giving the log permission to publish logs to it.

If the user creating the log doesn't own the bucket, or doesn't have the GetBucketPolicy and PutBucketPolicy permissions for the bucket, the log creation fails. In that case, the bucket owner must manually add the policy to the bucket and specify the log creator's AWS account ID. If the bucket receives logs from multiple accounts, you add a Resource element entry to the AWSLogDeliveryWrite policy statement for each account.

AccessDenied errors may appear in CloudTrail if the s3:ListBucket permission has not been granted to delivery.logs.amazonaws.com. To avoid these CloudTrail errors, you must grant s3:ListBucket to delivery.logs.amazonaws.com and include the Condition parameters shown with the s3:GetBucketAcl permission.

## KMS key permissions

If your logging destination uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key, you must give AWS WAF permission to use your KMS key. To do so, you add a key policy to the KMS key for your chosen destination.

## Access control on log files

Amazon S3 uses access control lists (ACLs) to manage access to the log files created by an AWS WAF log. By default, the bucket owner has FULL_CONTROL permissions on each log file. The log delivery owner, if different from the bucket owner, has no permissions by default. The log delivery account has READ and WRITE permissions.

# Exporting Log Data to Amazon S3

An export task can export all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group to an Amazon S3 bucket. Exporting log data to S3 buckets encrypted by AWS KMS is supported, but exporting to buckets encrypted with DSSE-KMS is not supported. An export task may take anywhere from a few seconds to a few hours, depending on the size of the data to export. The export task is created with the `aws logs create-export-task` command.

## Same-account or cross-account export

Which instructions apply depends on where the bucket is. If the S3 bucket is in the same account as the logs being exported, the same-account export instructions apply. If the S3 bucket is in a different account than the logs being exported, the cross-account export instructions apply.

## Bucket and Region requirements

AWS recommends using a bucket created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. However, an existing bucket can be used, in which case the bucket creation procedure can be skipped. The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export, because CloudWatch Logs does not support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region. In the create-bucket command, the LocationConstraint is the Region where log data is exported.

## Permissions required to create the export task

The user must sign in with sufficient permissions to create the export task. This means being signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role and having the permissions logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams and logs:DescribeLogGroups.

## Bucket access policy

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and its objects. The resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

The bucket policy enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to the bucket. It must specify the list of source accounts allowed to export log data to the bucket. The aws:SourceAccount key lists the accounts from which a user can export log data to the bucket. The aws:SourceArn key is the resource for which the action is taken, and it may be restricted to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the bucket is created in the policy.

The policy file must be created with a text editor, not the IAM console. The policy's Principal must be set to the endpoint of the Region where log data is exported. The put-bucket-policy command sets the policy as the bucket's access policy. The bucket owner has full permissions on all exported objects.

If an existing bucket is used, it may already have policies attached. In that case, the CloudWatch Logs access statements should be added to the existing policies, and the resulting set of permissions should be evaluated to ensure they are appropriate for users who access the bucket.

## SSE-KMS encrypted buckets

The SSE-KMS procedure is necessary only for buckets using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys, that is, when the destination bucket uses SSE-KMS encryption. In that procedure, a key_policy.json file is created and the key is created with `aws kms create-key`. The key policy lets the CloudWatch Logs service principal use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt. A bucketencryption.json file is then created and applied with `aws s3api put-bucket-encryption`.

## Additional requirements for cross-account export

For cross-account export, a new IAM policy must be created giving CloudWatch Logs s3:PutObject on the destination bucket in the destination account. This policy has additional requirements depending on the bucket configuration:

- If the destination bucket uses AWS KMS encryption, the IAM policy must also include kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt for the key resource.
- If ACLs are enabled on the destination bucket through S3 Object Ownership, the IAM policy must also include s3:PutObjectAcl.

Creating an export task for a cross-account export requires an IAM role with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess attached, as well as the IAM policy created for s3:PutObject. The cross-account bucket policy includes a statement allowing an IAM role in the log account to s3:PutObject, and the cross-account KMS key policy grants the export-task role kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

# Export log data to Amazon S3 using an export task

An export task can export all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group to an Amazon S3 bucket. Exporting log data to S3 buckets encrypted by AWS KMS is supported. Exporting to buckets encrypted with DSSE-KMS is not supported. The S3 bucket is either in the same account as the logs being exported or in a different account. If it is in the same account, the same-account export instructions apply. If it is in a different account, the cross-account export instructions apply.

## Before you begin

Complete the prerequisites that match your scenario before you create the export task.

**Both scenarios**
- An existing CloudWatch Logs log group to export (for example, `my-log-group`).

**Same account**
- A destination S3 bucket in the same Region as the log data. The steps are on this page.
- An S3 bucket policy that allows the CloudWatch Logs service principal to write objects and get the bucket ACL, with `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn` conditions. The steps are on this page.
- A signed-in IAM role or identity with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess and the permissions `logs:CreateExportTask`, `logs:CancelExportTask`, `logs:DescribeExportTasks`, `logs:DescribeLogStreams` and `logs:DescribeLogGroups`. The steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html.
- Only if the destination bucket uses SSE-KMS: a KMS key policy that allows CloudWatch Logs to use the key, and bucket default encryption configured with SSE-KMS. The steps are on this page.

**Cross-account**
- A destination S3 bucket in the destination account, in the same Region as the logs. The steps are on this page.
- An IAM identity policy that grants `s3:PutObject` on the destination bucket. Add `kms:GenerateDataKey` and `kms:Decrypt` if the bucket uses KMS, and `s3:PutObjectAcl` if ACLs are enabled. The steps are on this page.
- A signed-in IAM role with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess, the IAM policy you created, and the logs export permissions. The steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html.
- An S3 bucket policy on the destination bucket that allows CloudWatch Logs export, with the source accounts listed. The steps are on this page.

## Create or choose the destination bucket

AWS recommends using a bucket created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. You can instead use an existing bucket, in which case you can skip the bucket creation procedure.

The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export. CloudWatch Logs does not support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region. In the create-bucket command, the `LocationConstraint` is the Region where the log data is exported.

## Set permissions on the bucket

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and its objects. The resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

The bucket policy must specify the list of source accounts allowed to export log data to the bucket. The `aws:SourceAccount` key lists the accounts from which a user can export log data to the bucket. The `aws:SourceArn` key is the resource for which the action is taken. You can restrict it to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the bucket is created in the policy.

Create the policy file with a text editor, not the IAM console. Set the policy's `Principal` to the endpoint of the Region where the log data is exported. Then use the `put-bucket-policy` command to set the policy as the bucket's access policy. The bucket policy enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to the bucket, but only when the bucket is in the same Region as the log data. The bucket owner has full permissions on all exported objects.

An existing bucket may already have policies attached. If it does, add the CloudWatch Logs access statements to the existing policies. Then evaluate the resulting set of permissions to ensure they are appropriate for the users who access the bucket.

For a cross-account export, the bucket policy on the destination bucket also includes a statement allowing an IAM role in the log account to perform `s3:PutObject`. This statement applies only to cross-account exports.

## Configure SSE-KMS encryption (only if the bucket uses it)

This procedure is necessary only for buckets using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. Each of the following steps applies only when the destination bucket uses SSE-KMS encryption:

1. Create a `key_policy.json` file and create the key with `aws kms create-key`.
2. Create a `bucketencryption.json` file and apply it with `aws s3api put-bucket-encryption`.

The key policy lets the CloudWatch Logs service principal use `kms:GenerateDataKey` and `kms:Decrypt`. For a cross-account export to a bucket that uses SSE-KMS, the KMS key policy also grants the export-task role `kms:GenerateDataKey` and `kms:Decrypt`. This applies only when the bucket is in a different account and uses SSE-KMS.

## Create the IAM policy (cross-account only)

A new IAM policy must be created only for a cross-account export. It gives CloudWatch Logs `s3:PutObject` on the destination bucket in the destination account. Two additions depend on the bucket configuration:

- If the destination bucket uses AWS KMS encryption, the policy must also include `kms:GenerateDataKey` and `kms:Decrypt` for the key resource. This holds only when the bucket uses KMS and this policy exists.
- If ACLs are enabled on the destination bucket through S3 Object Ownership, the policy must also include `s3:PutObjectAcl`. This holds only when ACLs are enabled and this policy exists.

## Create the export task

Create the export task with the `aws logs create-export-task` command. You must sign in with sufficient permissions to create the export task, and the requirements depend on the scenario.

For a same-account export, the command works only when all of the following hold:
- You are signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role.
- You have the permissions `logs:CreateExportTask`, `logs:CancelExportTask`, `logs:DescribeExportTasks`, `logs:DescribeLogStreams` and `logs:DescribeLogGroups`.
- You have signed in with sufficient permissions to create the export task.

For a cross-account export, the command works only when all of the following hold:
- You use an IAM role with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess attached.
- You have the IAM policy created for `s3:PutObject`.
- You have the same logs permissions listed above.

An export task may take from a few seconds to a few hours, depending on the size of the data to export.

s3public.regen_doc:
New buckets block public access by default, and objects in a bucket with Block Public Access enabled cannot be read anonymously. This has a notable consequence for bucket policies: attaching a policy that grants s3:GetObject to everyone succeeds without any error, even while Block Public Access is on, so a successful attachment does not mean the objects are actually public.

The policy only takes effect if the bucket's Block Public Access settings are turned off. When they are off, and the bucket policy grants s3:GetObject to everyone, the policy takes effect and the objects in the bucket are readable by anyone.

Bucket-level settings are not the whole picture, however. If Block Public Access is enabled at the account level, the account-level setting overrides the bucket-level setting. In that case, the objects in the bucket stay private regardless of the bucket policy, even if the bucket's own settings have been turned off.

Static website hosting does not change any of this. Enabling it on the bucket does not alter the public access behavior, so if public access is still blocked, the website endpoint returns 403.

If you see a 403 from the website endpoint, check that both the account-level settings and the bucket-level settings allow public access. Checking the account setting first avoids spending a long time editing a policy that is being ignored.
